newsitem.title: USA: US bond group warns Congress about over-regulation.
newsitem.headline: US bond group warns Congress about over-regulation.

text.p: Public Securities Association on Wednesday urged Congress ensure that all off-exchange-traded government securities transactions remain clear of Commodity Futures Trading Commission oversight.

PSA Chairman John Meehan, a managing director at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell, told the House Agriculture Committee's risk management subcommittee that the government securities market is already adequately regulated under federal securities laws.
He asked that "special care be taken to avoid placing unnecessary and duplicative regulatory burdens on the government securities market."
Meehan's concerns came as the House panel is considering legislation that aims to spell out how much oversight the futures trading regulator has in the over-the-counter derivatives markets.

Many industry players fear the agency has over-stepped its regulatory bounds in several enforcement actions it has taken involving privately-negotiated transactions conducted off of a regulated futures exchange.
The bill being considered would also trim the CFTC's regulatory powers over the nation's futures markets as long as trades are limited to sophisticated players.

A similar measure is also being considered by the Senate Agriculture Committee. CFTC chairwoman Brooksley Born has warned repetitively that the legislation would destroy her agency's ability to effectively monitor fraud in the markets.
Represenatives from the nation's futures exchanges say the legislation is badly needed to help them better compete against the less-regulated over-the-counter markets.
